requirements.requirement: Run the worker under a dedicated unprivileged inventorysvc account.
requirements.summary: inventorysvc was created as system UID/GID 992, and the live worker process ran with that account, including after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Manage a functioning background worker as inventory-worker.
requirements.summary: inventory-worker.service was enabled and active; heartbeat counts increased before and after reboot, and recovery used a new process ID.

requirements.requirement: Confine the worker to a root-owned chroot with /var/lib/inventory as its only writable application directory.
requirements.summary: The chroot root was root-owned, the data directory belonged to inventorysvc, host /etc was hidden, writes to /var/lib/inventory succeeded, and writes to the chroot root and /usr/local/bin were denied both before and after reboot. Service properties corroborated the root directory, bind mount, strict protection, and sole read-write path.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with that platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64, and the implemented worker operated successfully using existing platform components.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged the reboot, demonstrated a changed boot identity, and directly verified recovered service, persistent data, continued heartbeats, and confinement. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: The configured nologin shell is established by the useradd command and baseline account absence, but the final account record was not printed in full.

The direct write-denial probes sampled the chroot root and executable tree rather than attempting every possible path; the broader conclusion is corroborated by ProtectSystem=strict and ReadWritePaths=/var/lib/inventory.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified in the chronological command review. Account, directory, runtime, SELinux, and unit changes directly implemented the requested service. The initial worker behavior was corrected after its startup warning; namespace probe writes were bounded validation artifacts, and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Final observations showed no failed services, new listeners, temporary-file residue attributable to the executor, or package-health damage.
